newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST-BUBOR FUTURES PARALLEL LAUNCH ON BSE, BCE.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST-BUBOR FUTURES PARALLEL LAUNCH ON BSE, BCE.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Tuesday that it will launch futures contracts for the one-and three-month Budapest Interbank Offered Rate (BUBOR) rates on September 19.
The date of introduction is in harmony with a similar step of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) which announced the start of trading in this instrument last week.

The BSE elected CIB Broker Kft as the specialist market maker for the three-month instrument until October 31, 1997, while it has not yet chosen market maker for the one-month rate, the BSE said in a statement.

By the launch of the two BUBOR rates, the BSE will increase the number of traded instruments in its futures section to seven. It also offers futures for BUX index, three-month discount Treasury bills, dollar, mark and ECU.
The financial section of the BCE -- which also trades traditional commodity goods -- will have 10 instruments when launching the BUBOR.
The BCE's financial section now offers seven currencies, dollar, mark, ECU, Swiss franc, Italian lira, sterling and yen, and three-month deposit interest rates.
The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) began calculating BUBOR, a composite of eight banks' rates, on August 1 with the aim of setting a benchmark rate for the interbank money market.
